key_insight: The paper replaces explicit finite-horizon quantum control synthesis with a variational optimization over a hardware-efficient quantum circuit that directly minimizes terminal infidelity to reach a target state.
engineering_relevance: This offers a near-term-friendly control strategy that is easier to implement on quantum hardware because it avoids problem-specific control-field design and uses standard circuit blocks and classical optimization.
method: Model terminal state transfer as a fidelity-based optimization problem over a fixed time horizon.
Use a hardware-efficient ansatz with alternating single-qubit rotations and entangling gates as a surrogate for the terminal evolution.
Optimize circuit parameters classically to minimize terminal infidelity without enforcing explicit reachability constraints.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical multi-qubit state-transfer benchmarks showing high-fidelity transfer and examining how performance changes with ansatz expressivity, optimization difficulty, and circuit depth.
watch_item: Performance may degrade as system size grows because higher expressivity can increase optimization complexity and depth requirements on noisy hardware.
paper_title: A Variational Surrogate Approach to Finite-Horizon Quantum Control via Hardware-Efficient Ansatz
